sections.content:
You know *como si* + imperfect subjunctive for unreal comparisons from B2 Unit 15 (*Habla como si lo supiera todo*). *¡Ni que* + imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive! is its punchy, ironic spoken cousin: it stands alone as a complete exclamation rejecting an absurd assumption ("As if...!").

Use the **imperfect subjunctive** (*-ra* or *-se*) to mock an ongoing or general assumption (*¡Ni que fuera millonario!* = "As if he were a millionaire!", *¡Ni que tuviéramos todo el día!* = "As if we had all day!"). Use the **pluperfect subjunctive** (*hubiera* / *hubiese* + participle) when the absurd assumption refers to a completed past event (*¡Ni que hubieras visto un fantasma!* = "As if you had seen a ghost!", *¡Ni que hubiera ocurrido un milagro!*).

Because *¡ni que...!* always presents the idea as blatantly unreal, it takes **only** the imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive—never the indicative (*¡Ni que es millonario!* ✗) and never the present subjunctive (*¡Ni que sea millonario!* ✗).

sections.title: Ironic exclamations with ¡Ni que...!
rows: Present / general assumption (*¡Ni que* + imperfect subjunctive)
*¡Ni que fuera millonario!* (As if he were a millionaire!)
Past / completed assumption (*¡Ni que* + pluperfect subjunctive)
*¡Ni que hubieras visto un fantasma!* (As if you had seen a ghost!)
Everyday spoken reaction to an exaggeration
*¡Ni que costara una fortuna!* (As if it cost a fortune!)
Compare with *como si* (B2 Unit 15, needs a main clause)
*Gasta como si fuera millonario.* vs *¡Ni que fuera millonario!*

items.spanish: Pide el menú más caro cada viernes: ¡ni que fuera millonario!
items.english: He orders the most expensive menu every Friday: as if he were a millionaire!

items.spanish: Te quedaste pálido por un correo: ¡ni que hubieras visto un fantasma!
items.english: You went pale over an email: as if you had seen a ghost!

items.spanish: Todo el mundo aplaudió porque llegó a la hora: ¡ni que hubiera hecho un milagro!
items.english: Everyone applauded because he arrived on time: as if he had performed a miracle!

items.spanish: No me tomes el pelo: ¡ni que ese chiste fuera tan bueno!
items.english: Don't pull my leg: as if that joke were that good!

sections.content: After *¡ni que...!*, never use the indicative (*¡ni que eres...* ✗) or the present subjunctive (*¡ni que seas...* ✗). Both *-ra* and *-se* forms are standard (*fuera / fuese*, *hubiera / hubiese*), with *-ra* much more common in everyday conversation.
